To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The zinc–nickel hybrid porphyrins were synthesized and characterized by NMR and UV/Vis spectroscopy.
we have successfully synthesized a hybrid porphyrins dimer using synthetic 4a-helix polypeptide and investigated the energy-transfer process of the hybrid dimer.
the synthetic polypeptide induced the formation of a hybrid porphyrins dimer containing zinc–nickel porphyrins, and that the energy transfer between the porphirins is efficient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a new type of hybrid porphrin dimer containing a zinc and nickel mesoporhyrin linked by a 4α-helical polypeptide.
the molecular design of a novel type of hybrid metalloporphyrin dimers, in which two porphyrins are connected by a polypeptide chain.

the development and characterization of synthetic polypeptides and proteins with defined secondary structures and the use of these materials for supramolecular chemistry, biomimetic catalysis and molecular recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthetic polypeptides can induce the formation of hybrid porphirin dimer and the energy-transfer between the zinc and nickel porphyrin.

the molecular assembly of zinc-nickel hybrid porphyrins using the synthetic 4α-Helical polypeptides was achieved and the energy transfer between the porphynins was induced by the presence of the helical polypeptide.
the molecular assembly of hybrid porphin dimer containing zinc mesoporphyrin and nickel mesotetra(pentafluorophenyl)porphyrin using synthetic 4-helix polypeptide was successful and efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we succeeded in the molecular assembly of hybrid porporhin dimer containing zinc-nickel porphyrin and the energy-transfer between the zinc-nickel hybrid porphyrins using synthetic α-helix polypeptide as a molecular scaffold.
the molecular assembly of zinc–nickel hybrid porphyrins using synthetic α-helix polypeptide was successfully achieved, and the energy transfer between porphyrin was observed.

the molecular assembly of zinc–nickel hybrid porphyrins was successfully achieved using 4α-helical polypeptides, which is expected to be applicable for the design of artificial photosynthetic systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy-transfer efficiency is significantly improved when the polypeptide is used as a linker, compared to the use of a simple alkane linker.
it is possible to control the energy transfer in a supramolecular assembly by changing the linker length between the porphynin dyes.
it is possible to control the distance between the metalloporphyrins in a supramolecular assembly by the design of the polypeptides.
